archetypes.name: scope-control
archetypes.rationale: The issue explicitly excludes item 2 and broader help/ship-driver work, so a specialist should catch over-scoped plan steps.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the plan against the staged issue scope and approved direction, looking for work that exceeds the three intended fixes or silently reintroduces excluded item 2. Check whether any proposed file edits, tests, or docs broaden behavior beyond additive DX/doc hardening. Flag missing scope boundaries where the plan could invite implementers to alter ship-path behavior or unrelated help contracts. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-wiring
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds a new shell harness plus Makefile shard and agent-lint reachability wiring, which is easy to under-specify.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect whether the test plan names all required harness integrations for the new append-execution-issue test and whether those integrations match existing repo conventions. Verify the plan accounts for Makefile target registration, shard coverage, sibling markdown documentation, and agent-lint exclusions without relying on unstated conventions. Look for missing or wrong targets that would let the new test exist but not run in relevant checks. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shell-contract-drift
archetypes.rationale: The fixes hinge on shell env propagation, source-vs-exec behavior, and Bash 3.2-safe CLI contracts across scripts and SKILL text.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the plan for mismatches between proposed shell contracts and the existing script/doc evidence, especially CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT derivation/export, fail_usage output shape, and lib-implement-round-cap direct execution. Check whether the SKILL.md snippets are specified precisely enough to avoid the original prompt-side shell mistakes while preserving sourced-library behavior. Flag any argv, exit-code, stdout, or environment assumptions that are not supported by the scoped files. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
